explanation: Unstable nuclei decay at random, but a huge population thins out predictably: every half-life t_half the count N halves, giving the smooth curve N = N0*e^(-lambda t) with lambda = ln2/t_half. Slide t_half to set the pace and N0 to set the starting count; the violet steps mark t_half, 2*t_half, ... where N drops to N0/2, N0/4, ... The red marker sweeps the curve and the readout shows how many nuclei remain and the percentage left at the current time.
bullets: Each half-life t_half cuts the count in half: N0 -> N0/2 -> N0/4 -> ...
Decay constant lambda = ln2/t_half sets the rate; bigger lambda = faster decay.
The decay is exponential, so it never quite reaches zero.
